# Export command

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1 — `forge export` writes one file

## Approach
The export command reads the job record and writes one file.
Line 2 of the approach: the flags are parsed first.
Line 3 of the approach: the output path defaults to the job dir.
Line 4 of the approach: an existing file is never overwritten.
Line 5 of the approach: the format is chosen by the extension.
Line 6 of the approach: JSON is the default format.
Line 7 of the approach: the writer streams large records.
Line 8 of the approach: the writer closes the file on error.
Line 9 of the approach: the exit code says what happened.
Line 10 of the approach: help text lists every flag.
Line 11 of the approach: unknown flags fail fast.
Line 12 of the approach: paths are resolved from the repo root.
Line 13 of the approach: relative paths stay inside the repo.
Line 14 of the approach: the command reports the written path.
Line 15 of the approach: the command reports the byte count.
Line 16 of the approach: the command never touches job state.
Line 17 of the approach: the record is read once.
Line 18 of the approach: the record is validated first.
Line 19 of the approach: a bad record stops the export.
Line 20 of the approach: the error names the field.
Line 21 of the approach: the field path is dotted.
Line 22 of the approach: arrays show their index.
Line 23 of the approach: the message is one line.
Line 24 of the approach: the JSON output is stable.
Line 25 of the approach: keys are sorted.
Line 26 of the approach: dates are ISO strings.
Line 27 of the approach: numbers stay numbers.
Line 28 of the approach: nulls are kept.
Line 29 of the approach: the file ends with a newline.
Line 30 of the approach: indentation is two spaces.
Line 31 of the approach: the CSV writer quotes commas.
Line 32 of the approach: the CSV writer quotes quotes.
Line 33 of the approach: the CSV header comes first.
Line 34 of the approach: columns follow the record order.
Line 35 of the approach: missing cells stay empty.
Line 36 of the approach: line endings are LF.
Line 37 of the approach: the YAML writer is not supported.
Line 38 of the approach: asking for YAML is an error.
Line 39 of the approach: the error lists the formats.
Line 40 of the approach: the formats list is sorted.
Line 41 of the approach: tests cover each format.
Line 42 of the approach: tests cover each error.
Line 43 of the approach: tests use a scratch directory.
Line 44 of the approach: tests never touch a real repo.
Line 45 of the approach: tests clean up after themselves.
Line 46 of the approach: docs describe each flag.
Line 47 of the approach: docs show one example.
Line 48 of the approach: the example uses a short id.
Line 49 of the approach: the example shows the output.
Line 50 of the approach: the changelog is left to the release.
Line 51 of the approach: the command is registered with the others.
Line 52 of the approach: the registry keeps alphabetical order.
Line 53 of the approach: the usage line lists the command.

Line 57 of the approach: completion lists the formats.

Line 59 of the approach: the command works offline.
Line 60 of the approach: the command needs no network.
Line 61 of the approach: the command needs no token.
Line 62 of the approach: the command runs in under a second.
Line 63 of the approach: large records still stream.
Line 64 of the approach: memory stays flat.
Line 65 of the approach: the stream has a high-water mark.
Line 66 of the approach: back-pressure is respected.
Line 67 of the approach: a closed pipe ends the export quietly.
Line 68 of the approach: the partial file is removed.
Line 69 of the approach: removal failures are reported.
Line 70 of the approach: the report is a warning.
Line 71 of the approach: warnings go to stderr.
Line 72 of the approach: results go to stdout.
Line 73 of the approach: --quiet silences warnings.
Line 74 of the approach: --quiet keeps errors.
